#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -q lva
#flux: --job-name=test
#flux: -o output.log

# The job requests 12 tasks on a single node.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: --ntasks-per-node=12

# The '--exclusive' flag requests the entire node for the job.
#flux: --exclusive

# The 'mpirun' command is replaced with 'flux run'.
# 'flux run' is the standard MPI launcher for Flux and will correctly start the 12 tasks requested.
# The MCA parameter is passed as an argument to 'flux run'.
flux run --omca fs_ufs_lock_algorithm 1 ./bin/saveBufferNonCollective

reasons: Validation failed at directive: --ntasks-per-node=12. For a single-node job, it is more common and robust to specify the total number of tasks, e.g., '-n 12'.
issues: The job requests 12 tasks but does not specify the number of CPUs per task (e.g., `-c N`). This defaults to 1 CPU per task. This is an appropriate allocation for a pure MPI job, but it may underutilize the node's resources if more than 12 cores are available and `--exclusive` has reserved the entire node.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash

# Execute job in the partition "lva" unless you have special requirements.
#SBATCH --partition=lva
# Name your job to be able to identify it later
#SBATCH --job-name test
# Redirect output stream to this file
#SBATCH --output=output.log
# Maximum number of tasks (=processes) to start in total
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=12
#SBATCH --nodes=1
# Maximum number of tasks (=processes) to start per node
# Enforce exclusive node allocation, do not share with other jobs
#SBATCH --exclusive

#!/bin/bash
mpirun --mca fs_ufs_lock_algorithm 1 -np 12 ./bin/saveBufferNonCollective
